cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Tell me you understand why six weeks of silence hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. For me, the silence didn't come with a repair notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Can you understand why I kept rewriting a message you'd never answered, trying to become easier to reply to?

mechanism: A controls which explanation counts as an adequate response and directs B to name the self-doubt produced by silence.
confusable: General blame for a broken phone concerns the event; D75 requires acknowledgment of the emotional cost to A.
comparison: A long unanswered-message exchange differs from the concert recording and a single missed event.
seedUse: Use D75-b repair notice and rewriting-message behavior; keep them as concrete personal evidence while making A adjudicate the reply.
